extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, covering English and German. It includes training, development, test, and unannotated data files for each language. Named entities are annotated for four types: persons (PER), organizations (ORG), locations (LOC), and miscellaneous names (MISC). English data is sourced from the Reuters Corpus (news stories August 1996–December 1996) and German data from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (Frankfurter Rundschau, August 1992). The dataset contains over 200,000 tokens per language in the training sets and millions of tokens in the unannotated data.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.publisher: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task Organizers, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For training and development sets, ten days of data from end of August 1996 were used; for the test set, texts from December 1996 were used. German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau. Training, development, and test sets were from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. Raw unannotated data for English covers September 1996 and for German covers September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English data: Reuters Corpus (http://www.reuters.com/researchandstandards/), consisting of Reuters news stories. German data: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (http://www.ldc.upenn.edu/), specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to December 1996 (training/development from end of August 1996; test from December 1996; unannotated from September 1996). German: August 1992 to December 1992 (training/development/test from one week at end of August 1992; unannotated from September to December 1992).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The IOB tagging scheme (originally by Ramshaw and Marcus, 1995) was used. Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another, only the top-level entity was annotated. The B-XXX tag is used for the first word of a second consecutive entity of the same type.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and chunker were applied to the raw data. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). German data was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995). Data format: one word per line with empty lines representing sentence boundaries; each line contains four fields: word, part-of-speech tag, chunk tag, and named entity tag.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not in the other categories (persons, organizations, locations), including adjectives like 'Italian' and events like '1000 Lakes Rally'.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT (Memory-Based Tagger) by Daelemans et al. (2002) for English POS tagging and chunking; Treetagger (Schmid, 1995) for German lemmatization, POS tagging, and chunking.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The English data is sourced exclusively from Reuters news stories and the German data from a single newspaper (Frankfurter Rundschau), which may limit the diversity of language and named entity types represented.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers only two languages (English and German). Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; embedded named entities are not fully annotated. The MISC category is described as very diverse. Better gazetteers are available for English than German, which may affect system performance comparisons across languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (parameter tuning), and testing of named entity recognition systems. The dataset was specifically designed for the CoNLL-2003 shared task on language-independent named entity recognition. Unannotated data was provided to encourage semi-supervised and unsupervised learning approaches. Evaluation is performed using F-beta=1 (F1) score based on exact match of named entities.
